title: Modularity, functions & procedures
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: Which loop is most suitable when the number of repetitions is known in advance?
questions.feedback: It is commonly used for count-controlled iteration.

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: In C#, what does && mean, and when is the whole expression true?
questions.feedback: The whole expression is true only when both Boolean expressions are true.

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: What is the largest unsigned 8-bit denary value?
questions.feedback: Eight bits give 256 patterns, representing values 0–255.

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: A program reads a mark, repeats through five scores and uses if to count passes. Name the three programming constructs present.
questions.feedback: Instructions happen in order, a loop repeats code, and if chooses whether the pass counter changes.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: Modularity — Breaking a program into smaller, separate components.
Subroutine — A named block of code that can be called to perform a task.
Method — The C# term used for the functions and procedures in this lesson.
Function — A subroutine that returns a value.
Procedure — A subroutine that does not return a value.
Return value — The data sent back from a function to its caller.

blocks.title: Modularity breaks a problem into parts
blocks.text: A large program is easier to understand when separate jobs are placed in separate subroutines.

blocks.title: A procedure performs a job
blocks.text: A C# procedure-style method uses void because it does not return a value to the caller.

blocks.title: A function returns a value
blocks.text: The return type replaces void . A return statement sends the result back to the calling code.

blocks.title: Parameters receive data
blocks.text: A parameter is the named input in the method definition. An argument is the actual value supplied when the method is called.

blocks.title: Worked example · Build an IsEven function
blocks.text: Create a function that accepts a whole number and returns true when it is even. The result is data, so this should be a function .
